observations.text: Preview banner: “Evaluation preview · learning history and analytics are not saved.”
Prediction: real areas? “Greenland about 15× Congo”, “Greenland about 1× Congo”, “Congo about 4× Greenland”; chose 15× and locked.
At 73°N: 15.4×; clicked Slide to equator: 0.9×; Equal-area map retained 0.9× and changed orange compass line from straight to bent.
Reveal: “Not quite: it was ‘Greenland about 1× Congo’”; 2.17 vs 2.34 million km²; “The land never changed; the map did.”
Reveal links Mercator latitude stretching to sailing/angles and states “No flat map can keep both.”

prediction.reason: Clear real-versus-drawn commitment separates plausible size beliefs.

interaction.reason: Moving latitude and switching projection visibly contrast area and compass bearing.

payoff.reason: Reveal resolves prediction using observed ratios and explains the angle/area limit.

clarity.reason: Explicit instructions and Seen record made the sequence followable.

transfer.reason: Map choice is linked to area comparison versus compass-bearing navigation.

accessibility.reason: No sufficient multi-mode accessibility checks; D slider Home key is only a partial keyboard observation.
evidence: Observed DOM accessible names, desktop screenshots; no comprehensive check.

surprise.reason: Committed 15× belief is reversed by the equatorial 0.9× result.

visualExplanation.reason: Map shape, ratio and bearing-line changes carry two linked contrasts.

playfulness.reason: Slider and projection toggle invite reversible experimentation.

practicalValue.reason: Projection choice supports geographic comparison and navigation.

depth.reason: Latitude distortion and bearing/area trade-off are distinct mechanisms.

complexity.reason: Compare ratios, understand latitude movement, and distinguish area from compass bearing.
complexity.boundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparing numbers and familiar household objects; no domain theory assumed.

whyCool: Moving Greenland south shrinks its drawn ratio from 15.4× to 0.9× while the land stays the same.
caveat: No reset, phone viewport or accessibility suite tested.
